See also: [1950 French Annapurna expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_French_Annapurna_expedition "1950 French Annapurna expedition") and [1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_British_Annapurna_South_Face_expedition "1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition")

Annapurna I was the first 8,000-metre (26,200 ft) peak to be climbed.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-econdailychart-15)[Maurice Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Herzog "Maurice Herzog") and [Louis Lachenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Lachenal "Louis Lachenal"), of the [French Annapurna expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_French_Annapurna_expedition "1950 French Annapurna expedition") led by Herzog (including [Lionel Terray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Terray "Lionel Terray"), [Gaston Rébuffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_R%C3%A9buffat "Gaston Rébuffat"), [Marcel Ichac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcel_Ichac "Marcel Ichac"), [Jean Couzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Couzy "Jean Couzy"), Marcel Schatz, Jacques Oudot, Francis de Noyelle), reached the summit on 3 June 1950.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-16) Ichac made a documentary of the expedition, called _Victoire sur l'Annapurna_. Its summit was the [highest one ever attained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_altitude_record_(mountaineering) "World altitude record (mountaineering)") at the time, but not the highest climb; higher non-summit points – at least 8,500 metres (27,900 ft) – had already been attained on [Mount Everest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Everest "Mount Everest") in the 1920s.

The [south face of Annapurna was first climbed in 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_British_Annapurna_South_Face_expedition "1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition") by [Don Whillans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Whillans "Don Whillans") and [Dougal Haston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dougal_Haston "Dougal Haston") also without using supplementary oxygen, members of a [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") expedition led by [Chris Bonington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Bonington "Chris Bonington") that included [Ian Clough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Clough "Ian Clough"), who was killed by a falling [serac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serac "Serac") during the descent.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1971-17) They were, however, beaten to the second ascent of Annapurna by a matter of days by a [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") expedition whose climbing team was led by then-Captain [Henry Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Day_(British_Army_officer) "Henry Day (British Army officer)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-18)

In 1978, the [American Women's Himalayan Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Women's_Himalayan_Expedition "American Women's Himalayan Expedition"), a team led by [Arlene Blum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlene_Blum "Arlene Blum"), became the first [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") team to climb Annapurna I. The first summit team, composed of [Vera Komarkova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Komarkova "Vera Komarkova") and [Irene Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irene_Beardsley "Irene Beardsley"), and [Sherpas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherpa_people "Sherpa people") Mingma Tsering and Chewang Ringjing, reached the top at 3:30 pm on 15 October 1978. Komarkova and Miller were the first women ever to reach the summit of the mountain.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-out-19) The second summit team, [Alison Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz "Alison Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz") and [Vera Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Watson "Vera Watson"), died during this climb.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-20)

In 1981 Polish expedition Zakopane Alpine Club set a new route on Annapurna I Central (8051 m). [Maciej Berbeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maciej_Berbeka "Maciej Berbeka") and Bogusław Probulski reached the summit on 23 May 1981. The route called Zakopiańczyków Way was recognized as the best achievement of the Himalayan season in 1981.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 3 February 1987, [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland")[climbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climbing "Climbing")[Jerzy Kukuczka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Kukuczka "Jerzy Kukuczka") and [Artur Hajzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artur_Hajzer "Artur Hajzer") made the first winter ascent of Annapurna I.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-21)

The first solo ascent of the south face was made in October 2007 by Slovenian climber [Tomaž Humar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toma%C5%BE_Humar "Tomaž Humar");[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-russianclimb-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-oustideaway-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-bergsteigen-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-climbing.de-25) he climbed to Roc Noir and then to Annapurna East (8,047m).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-rus-26)

Swiss climber [Ueli Steck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ueli_Steck "Ueli Steck") claimed to have soloed the Lafaille route,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-rus-26) on the main and highest part of the face, on 8 and 9 October 2013.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-27) This was his third attempt on the route and has been called "one of the most impressive Himalayan climbs in history",[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-28) with Steck taking 28 hours to make the trip from Base Camp to summit and back again.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-29) There are significant doubts about this claim.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-30)

### Fatality rate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annapurna&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Fatality rate")]

Along with K2 and [Nanga Parbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanga_Parbat "Nanga Parbat"), Annapurna I has consistently ranked as one of the most dangerous of the principal eight-thousander summits. Climbers killed on the peak include Britons [Ian Clough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Clough "Ian Clough") in 1970,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1971-17) and [Alex MacIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_MacIntyre "Alex MacIntyre") in 1982, Frenchman Pierre Béghin in 1992,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1993-31) Kazakh [Anatoli Boukreev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoli_Boukreev "Anatoli Boukreev") in 1997, Spaniard [Iñaki Ochoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I%C3%B1aki_Ochoa_de_Olza "Iñaki Ochoa de Olza") in 2008,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-32) Korean [Park Young-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Young-seok "Park Young-seok") in 2011[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-33) and the Finn [Samuli Mansikka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuli_Mansikka "Samuli Mansikka") in 2015.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-34)

**Annapurna** ([/ˌ æ n ə ˈ p ʊər n ə ˌ-ˈ p ɜːr-/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English");[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-7)[Nepali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepali_language "Nepali language"): [अन्नपूर्ण](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A3 "wikt:अन्नपूर्ण")) is a [mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain "Mountain") situated in the [Annapurna mountain range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_(mountain_range) "Annapurna (mountain range)") of [Gandaki Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandaki_Province "Gandaki Province"), north-central [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal "Nepal"). It is the [10th highest mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest_mountains_on_Earth "List of highest mountains on Earth") in the world at 8,091 metres (26,545 ft) above sea level and is well known for the difficulty and danger involved in its ascent.

[Maurice Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Herzog "Maurice Herzog") led a [French expedition to its summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_French_Annapurna_expedition "1950 French Annapurna expedition") through the north face in 1950, making it the first [eight-thousander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight-thousander "Eight-thousander") to be successfully climbed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-8) The entire massif and surrounding area are protected within the 7,629-square-kilometre (2,946 mi 2)[Annapurna Conservation Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_Conservation_Area "Annapurna Conservation Area"), the first and largest conservation area in Nepal. The Annapurna Conservation Area is home to several world-class [treks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpacking_(wilderness) "Backpacking (wilderness)"), including [Annapurna Sanctuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_Sanctuary "Annapurna Sanctuary") and [Annapurna Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_Circuit "Annapurna Circuit").

For decades, Annapurna I held the highest fatality-to-summit rate of all principal eight-thousander summits; it has, however, seen great climbing successes in recent years, with a current fatality rate of approximately 13.42% (75 deaths from 559 ascents), according to [Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-gwr-annapurna-9) The mountain still poses grave threats to climbers through avalanche danger, unpredictable weather and the extremely steep and committing nature of its climbing routes, in particular its 3,000-metre (9,800 ft) south face, renowned as one of the most difficult climbs in the world.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-10) It is also a dangerous peak for trekkers, as in the case of [a 2014 snowstorm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Nepal_snowstorm_disaster "2014 Nepal snowstorm disaster") near it and Dhaulagiri which killed at least 43 people. As of February 2025, 559 people had reached the summit of Annapurna I, while 75 had died in the attempt.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-gwr-annapurna-9)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annapurna&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The mountain is named after [Annapurna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_(goddess) "Annapurna (goddess)"), the Hindu goddess of food and nourishment, who is said to reside there. The name Annapurna is derived from the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit")-language words _purna_ ("filled") and _anna_ ("food"), and can be translated as "everlasting food".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-Loar2011-11) Many streams descending from the slopes of the Annapurna Massif provide water for the agricultural fields and pastures located at lower elevations.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-Frankel2003-12)

## Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annapurna&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geology")]

Annapurna Mountain consists of a few-kilometre-thick stack of early [Paleozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleozoic "Paleozoic")[sedimentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary "Sedimentary") and [metasedimentary rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metasedimentary_rock "Metasedimentary rock") of the [Tethyan Himalayan Sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-collisional_Himalaya "Pre-collisional Himalaya") that steeply [dips northward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_and_dip "Strike and dip"). From top to bottom these sedimentary rocks consist of [Ordovician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordovician "Ordovician")[limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone"), [dolomite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolomite_(rock) "Dolomite (rock)"), calc-[schist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schist "Schist"), [shale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shale "Shale"), and [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone "Sandstone") of the Nilgiri Formation; [Cambrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambrian "Cambrian")[psammite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psammite "Psammite"), [marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marble "Marble"), and sandstone of the Annapurna Yellow Formation; and Cambrian [pelitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelitic "Pelitic") and the highly deformed, semipelitic schists of the Sanctuary Formation. These northerly tilted (dipping) layers of sedimentary rocks are the northern [limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticline "Anticline") of the overturned Nilgiri [Anticline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticline "Anticline"). The summit of Annapurna consists of the Nilgiri Formation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-GodinOthers1981a-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-ParsonOthers2016a-14)

Tethyan Himalayan Sequence consists of a 11-kilometre (6.8 mi) thick pile of [Neoproterozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoproterozoic "Neoproterozoic") to [Mesozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesozoic "Mesozoic") sedimentary rocks that accumulated within a prehistoric [continental shelf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf "Continental shelf"). This continental shelf was located along the northern shore of the Indian subcontinent and submerged beneath southern margin of the prehistoric [Tethys Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_Ocean "Tethys Ocean") prior its collision with Asia. The collision of India and Asia during the [Himalayan orogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayan_orogeny "Himalayan orogeny") incorporated this continental shelf into the Himalayan Mountains as a thin, [fault-bounded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_(geology) "Fault (geology)") tectonic package of rocks that outcrops continuously for more than 2,000-kilometre (1,200 mi) along the length of the Himalayan Mountains.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-GodinOthers1981a-13)

See also: [1950 French Annapurna expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_French_Annapurna_expedition "1950 French Annapurna expedition") and [1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_British_Annapurna_South_Face_expedition "1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition")

Annapurna I was the first 8,000-metre (26,200 ft) peak to be climbed.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-econdailychart-15)[Maurice Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Herzog "Maurice Herzog") and [Louis Lachenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Lachenal "Louis Lachenal"), of the [French Annapurna expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_French_Annapurna_expedition "1950 French Annapurna expedition") led by Herzog (including [Lionel Terray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Terray "Lionel Terray"), [Gaston Rébuffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_R%C3%A9buffat "Gaston Rébuffat"), [Marcel Ichac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcel_Ichac "Marcel Ichac"), [Jean Couzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Couzy "Jean Couzy"), Marcel Schatz, Jacques Oudot, Francis de Noyelle), reached the summit on 3 June 1950.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-16) Ichac made a documentary of the expedition, called _Victoire sur l'Annapurna_. Its summit was the [highest one ever attained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_altitude_record_(mountaineering) "World altitude record (mountaineering)") at the time, but not the highest climb; higher non-summit points – at least 8,500 metres (27,900 ft) – had already been attained on [Mount Everest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Everest "Mount Everest") in the 1920s.

The [south face of Annapurna was first climbed in 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_British_Annapurna_South_Face_expedition "1970 British Annapurna South Face expedition") by [Don Whillans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Whillans "Don Whillans") and [Dougal Haston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dougal_Haston "Dougal Haston") also without using supplementary oxygen, members of a [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") expedition led by [Chris Bonington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Bonington "Chris Bonington") that included [Ian Clough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Clough "Ian Clough"), who was killed by a falling [serac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serac "Serac") during the descent.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1971-17) They were, however, beaten to the second ascent of Annapurna by a matter of days by a [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") expedition whose climbing team was led by then-Captain [Henry Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Day_(British_Army_officer) "Henry Day (British Army officer)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-18)

In 1978, the [American Women's Himalayan Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Women's_Himalayan_Expedition "American Women's Himalayan Expedition"), a team led by [Arlene Blum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlene_Blum "Arlene Blum"), became the first [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") team to climb Annapurna I. The first summit team, composed of [Vera Komarkova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Komarkova "Vera Komarkova") and [Irene Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irene_Beardsley "Irene Beardsley"), and [Sherpas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherpa_people "Sherpa people") Mingma Tsering and Chewang Ringjing, reached the top at 3:30 pm on 15 October 1978. Komarkova and Miller were the first women ever to reach the summit of the mountain.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-out-19) The second summit team, [Alison Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz "Alison Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz") and [Vera Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Watson "Vera Watson"), died during this climb.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-20)

In 1981 Polish expedition Zakopane Alpine Club set a new route on Annapurna I Central (8051 m). [Maciej Berbeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maciej_Berbeka "Maciej Berbeka") and Bogusław Probulski reached the summit on 23 May 1981. The route called Zakopiańczyków Way was recognized as the best achievement of the Himalayan season in 1981.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 3 February 1987, [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland")[climbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climbing "Climbing")[Jerzy Kukuczka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Kukuczka "Jerzy Kukuczka") and [Artur Hajzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artur_Hajzer "Artur Hajzer") made the first winter ascent of Annapurna I.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-21)

The first solo ascent of the south face was made in October 2007 by Slovenian climber [Tomaž Humar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toma%C5%BE_Humar "Tomaž Humar");[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-russianclimb-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-oustideaway-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-bergsteigen-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-climbing.de-25) he climbed to Roc Noir and then to Annapurna East (8,047m).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-rus-26)

Swiss climber [Ueli Steck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ueli_Steck "Ueli Steck") claimed to have soloed the Lafaille route,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-rus-26) on the main and highest part of the face, on 8 and 9 October 2013.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-27) This was his third attempt on the route and has been called "one of the most impressive Himalayan climbs in history",[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-28) with Steck taking 28 hours to make the trip from Base Camp to summit and back again.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-29) There are significant doubts about this claim.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-30)

### Fatality rate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annapurna&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Fatality rate")]

Along with K2 and [Nanga Parbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanga_Parbat "Nanga Parbat"), Annapurna I has consistently ranked as one of the most dangerous of the principal eight-thousander summits. Climbers killed on the peak include Britons [Ian Clough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Clough "Ian Clough") in 1970,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1971-17) and [Alex MacIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_MacIntyre "Alex MacIntyre") in 1982, Frenchman Pierre Béghin in 1992,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-AAJ1993-31) Kazakh [Anatoli Boukreev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoli_Boukreev "Anatoli Boukreev") in 1997, Spaniard [Iñaki Ochoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I%C3%B1aki_Ochoa_de_Olza "Iñaki Ochoa de Olza") in 2008,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-32) Korean [Park Young-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Young-seok "Park Young-seok") in 2011[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-33) and the Finn [Samuli Mansikka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuli_Mansikka "Samuli Mansikka") in 2015.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapurna_I#cite_note-34)

_**Pravegaya**_ (English: velocity ) is a 2015 [Sri Lankan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka") Sinhala action thriller film directed by Donald Jayantha and produced by Sadesh Kumar. It stars [Hemal Ranasinghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemal_Ranasinghe "Hemal Ranasinghe"), and [Udari Perera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udari_Perera "Udari Perera") in lead roles along with [Jayalath Manoratne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayalath_Manoratne "Jayalath Manoratne"), [Pubudu Chathuranga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pubudu_Chathuranga "Pubudu Chathuranga"), and [Jackson Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Anthony "Jackson Anthony") in supporting roles. Music for the film is done by [Bathiya and Santhush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathiya_and_Santhush "Bathiya and Santhush").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-2) It is the 1228th Sri Lankan film in the [Sinhala cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Sri_Lanka "Cinema of Sri Lanka").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-3) The film is a remake of 2007 film _[Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan\_(2007\_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)")_.

## Plot

Hemal is a happy-go-lucky middle-class family guy who spends time playing carrom in the streets with his friends Janith and Kumar. His father and he keep falling into minor misunderstandings, and he indulges in a hopeless romance with a strange girl who he meets at a bus stop. When he is caught in the act of stealing a pittance from his father for booze with his friends, Hemal questions his father’s responsibility towards his upbringing. His angry father gives Hemal some of his savings and tells him to do something with his life. Hemal purchases a [TVS Apache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVS_Apache "TVS Apache") bike instead and finds a job. The bike eventually saves his life from a freak incident and gets lost, subjecting him to interminable anguish as he searches for his bike. When his family members asks him about his bike, he tells them that he has given it for dealer service.

Hemal comes into conflict with the underworld when he witnesses a brutal murder planned by a gang of Smuggling don, Brando and his accomplices. Hemal finds out that his bike was stolen by a petty bike thief who turns out to be in connection with Brando's younger brother G.J.I. Hemal traces down the culprit as Chamara and hands him over to the local police station. A formal complaint is lodged on Chamara on the same night. Later that night Hemal confesses to his family that his bike was stolen. His Family is very upset with him due to his irresponsible behavior. The next morning G.J.I visits Hemal's residence and threatens him to withdraw the complaint against Chamara. When Hemal refuses, a fight breaks between Hemal and G.J.I, where G.J.I is joined by few of his accomplices, Hemal manages to fight them all and leaves G.J.I beaten and embarrassed among the public. Brando returns home in bail after a murder charge. When he finds out what happened to G.J.I, he gets furious and sends his henchmen to kill Hemal without knowing the reason for his brother's embarrassment. Meanwhile, Hemal, along with his friend and auto driver Kumar, meets Brando at his own residence. G.J.I is not home at that time. Hemal tells the truth to Brando but refuses to believe that his brother G.J.I and his men stole his bike. After hearing from his close ally Wasanth, Brando believes Hemal, apologizing for what happened and promises Hemal that he will do whatever he can to get his bike back. But it was too late for Hemal's father Jayalath Manoratne who receives the attack from G.J.I's men. He was admitted in a hospital and Hemal breaks down after knowing that his father may never walk again after his right leg is paralysed by the attack. Brando, G.J.I and their men visit Hemal to condole and apologize for what happened this time. Hemal turns down the apology and again an immediate fight was about to break between Hemal and G.J.I before Brando separates them both. Although he wants to stay away, Hemal invariably gets dragged into rubbing shoulders with the criminals who now target his family to seek revenge.

Hemal's bike was caught by Anti-Narcotics wing police and they nab Hemal suspecting him of Drug-smuggling in his bike. They release him after Hemal tells them that his bike was stolen and shows them his FIR copy. But he doesn't tell them about G.J.I or Brando. Now Hemal learns that his bike was stolen by Brando's men to escape from a murder scene but it was G.J.I who smuggled drugs in his bike's petrol tank. Hemal loses his job as an employee in his workplace since his bike was a source of transportation, and as he was kept at police custody for one night. Hemal also gets despair from Udari's father for being involved unwillingly with Brando's men. G.J.I makes one more attempt at Hemal's life but he was snubbed again by Hemal. Brando becomes unhappy about this and warns him to quit smuggling if he ever gets in Hemal's business anymore. G.J.I accuses Brando of being a non-caring brother and Out intervenes and warns G.J.I to mind his language. Then surprisingly Brando himself comes in support of his brother to lash out at Wasantha. Wasantha separates briefly from Brando after this conflict. The next day Brando and G.J.I gets attacked by unknown gangsters when they were traveling in their car outside the city. Brando asks his brother to stay inside the car and handles the killers on his own. He gets brutally injured though only to find out that he's been stabbed on back by his own Brother G.J.I. The attack was arranged by G.J.I himself to kill Brando. G.J.I delivers the killer blow before telling that Brando is too complacent of Hemal and he's going to kill him after killing Brando. Brando dies. G.J.I creates a scene among Brando's family, henchmen and Wasantha that he's not aware of who launched the assault on Brando. Wasantha gets furious and vows to kill every enemy of his mentor Brando including Hemal.

Hemal gets his bike back and was relieved for a brief time before coming to know what is going on and G.J.I is after him and his family. He first goes to save Udari. After securing her, he goes to save his family. He thinks the only way to stop this is to confront G.J.I himself. he takes down all the men sent by G.J.I who comes in his way. Meanwhile, Hemal's family were chased down in Mahen's auto-rickshaw by G.J.I's men. Hemal finds G.J.I hiding in an Ice-factory and engages him in a fight. Hemal gets G.J.I under the knife, threatening him to ask his men to leave Hemal's family. G.J.I does so. When Heaml is about to leave, G.J.I provokes him to continue the fight until death. Hemal manages to dodge G.J.I's swing of his knife and gets a steel rod to fatally knock down G.J.I. Wasantha arrives at the scene. Surprisingly he tells G.J.I that he discovered G.J.I's conspiracy of killing Brando before G.J.I dies. Hemal leaves the scene in his much beloved Apache bike.

## Background

_Pravegeya_ is an official sinhala remake of the Indian Tamil film [Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan_(2007_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)") which starred [Dhanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhanush "Dhanush") and [Divya Spandana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Spandana "Divya Spandana") in its lead roles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4) It is considered to be the most expensive and the biggest budgeted film ever done in Sri Lanka.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Jacqueline Fernandez was cast into a lead role in September 2011 for [Rs.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lankan_rupee "Sri Lankan rupee")8 million which is considered as the highest budget ever been paid to an actress in Sri Lanka,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] however, the production met initial difficulties when Fernandez failed to appear on her initial shooting date. Filming was done in Sri Lanka at locations including [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [Nuwara Eliya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuwara_Eliya "Nuwara Eliya") and [Galle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galle "Galle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4)

_**Pravegaya**_ (English: velocity ) is a 2015 [Sri Lankan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka") Sinhala action thriller film directed by Donald Jayantha and produced by Sadesh Kumar. It stars [Hemal Ranasinghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemal_Ranasinghe "Hemal Ranasinghe"), and [Udari Perera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udari_Perera "Udari Perera") in lead roles along with [Jayalath Manoratne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayalath_Manoratne "Jayalath Manoratne"), [Pubudu Chathuranga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pubudu_Chathuranga "Pubudu Chathuranga"), and [Jackson Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Anthony "Jackson Anthony") in supporting roles. Music for the film is done by [Bathiya and Santhush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathiya_and_Santhush "Bathiya and Santhush").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-2) It is the 1228th Sri Lankan film in the [Sinhala cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Sri_Lanka "Cinema of Sri Lanka").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-3) The film is a remake of 2007 film _[Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan\_(2007\_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)")_.

## Plot

Hemal is a happy-go-lucky middle-class family guy who spends time playing carrom in the streets with his friends Janith and Kumar. His father and he keep falling into minor misunderstandings, and he indulges in a hopeless romance with a strange girl who he meets at a bus stop. When he is caught in the act of stealing a pittance from his father for booze with his friends, Hemal questions his father’s responsibility towards his upbringing. His angry father gives Hemal some of his savings and tells him to do something with his life. Hemal purchases a [TVS Apache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVS_Apache "TVS Apache") bike instead and finds a job. The bike eventually saves his life from a freak incident and gets lost, subjecting him to interminable anguish as he searches for his bike. When his family members asks him about his bike, he tells them that he has given it for dealer service.

Hemal comes into conflict with the underworld when he witnesses a brutal murder planned by a gang of Smuggling don, Brando and his accomplices. Hemal finds out that his bike was stolen by a petty bike thief who turns out to be in connection with Brando's younger brother G.J.I. Hemal traces down the culprit as Chamara and hands him over to the local police station. A formal complaint is lodged on Chamara on the same night. Later that night Hemal confesses to his family that his bike was stolen. His Family is very upset with him due to his irresponsible behavior. The next morning G.J.I visits Hemal's residence and threatens him to withdraw the complaint against Chamara. When Hemal refuses, a fight breaks between Hemal and G.J.I, where G.J.I is joined by few of his accomplices, Hemal manages to fight them all and leaves G.J.I beaten and embarrassed among the public. Brando returns home in bail after a murder charge. When he finds out what happened to G.J.I, he gets furious and sends his henchmen to kill Hemal without knowing the reason for his brother's embarrassment. Meanwhile, Hemal, along with his friend and auto driver Kumar, meets Brando at his own residence. G.J.I is not home at that time. Hemal tells the truth to Brando but refuses to believe that his brother G.J.I and his men stole his bike. After hearing from his close ally Wasanth, Brando believes Hemal, apologizing for what happened and promises Hemal that he will do whatever he can to get his bike back. But it was too late for Hemal's father Jayalath Manoratne who receives the attack from G.J.I's men. He was admitted in a hospital and Hemal breaks down after knowing that his father may never walk again after his right leg is paralysed by the attack. Brando, G.J.I and their men visit Hemal to condole and apologize for what happened this time. Hemal turns down the apology and again an immediate fight was about to break between Hemal and G.J.I before Brando separates them both. Although he wants to stay away, Hemal invariably gets dragged into rubbing shoulders with the criminals who now target his family to seek revenge.

Hemal's bike was caught by Anti-Narcotics wing police and they nab Hemal suspecting him of Drug-smuggling in his bike. They release him after Hemal tells them that his bike was stolen and shows them his FIR copy. But he doesn't tell them about G.J.I or Brando. Now Hemal learns that his bike was stolen by Brando's men to escape from a murder scene but it was G.J.I who smuggled drugs in his bike's petrol tank. Hemal loses his job as an employee in his workplace since his bike was a source of transportation, and as he was kept at police custody for one night. Hemal also gets despair from Udari's father for being involved unwillingly with Brando's men. G.J.I makes one more attempt at Hemal's life but he was snubbed again by Hemal. Brando becomes unhappy about this and warns him to quit smuggling if he ever gets in Hemal's business anymore. G.J.I accuses Brando of being a non-caring brother and Out intervenes and warns G.J.I to mind his language. Then surprisingly Brando himself comes in support of his brother to lash out at Wasantha. Wasantha separates briefly from Brando after this conflict. The next day Brando and G.J.I gets attacked by unknown gangsters when they were traveling in their car outside the city. Brando asks his brother to stay inside the car and handles the killers on his own. He gets brutally injured though only to find out that he's been stabbed on back by his own Brother G.J.I. The attack was arranged by G.J.I himself to kill Brando. G.J.I delivers the killer blow before telling that Brando is too complacent of Hemal and he's going to kill him after killing Brando. Brando dies. G.J.I creates a scene among Brando's family, henchmen and Wasantha that he's not aware of who launched the assault on Brando. Wasantha gets furious and vows to kill every enemy of his mentor Brando including Hemal.

Hemal gets his bike back and was relieved for a brief time before coming to know what is going on and G.J.I is after him and his family. He first goes to save Udari. After securing her, he goes to save his family. He thinks the only way to stop this is to confront G.J.I himself. he takes down all the men sent by G.J.I who comes in his way. Meanwhile, Hemal's family were chased down in Mahen's auto-rickshaw by G.J.I's men. Hemal finds G.J.I hiding in an Ice-factory and engages him in a fight. Hemal gets G.J.I under the knife, threatening him to ask his men to leave Hemal's family. G.J.I does so. When Heaml is about to leave, G.J.I provokes him to continue the fight until death. Hemal manages to dodge G.J.I's swing of his knife and gets a steel rod to fatally knock down G.J.I. Wasantha arrives at the scene. Surprisingly he tells G.J.I that he discovered G.J.I's conspiracy of killing Brando before G.J.I dies. Hemal leaves the scene in his much beloved Apache bike.

## Background

_Pravegeya_ is an official sinhala remake of the Indian Tamil film [Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan_(2007_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)") which starred [Dhanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhanush "Dhanush") and [Divya Spandana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Spandana "Divya Spandana") in its lead roles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4) It is considered to be the most expensive and the biggest budgeted film ever done in Sri Lanka.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Jacqueline Fernandez was cast into a lead role in September 2011 for [Rs.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lankan_rupee "Sri Lankan rupee")8 million which is considered as the highest budget ever been paid to an actress in Sri Lanka,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] however, the production met initial difficulties when Fernandez failed to appear on her initial shooting date. Filming was done in Sri Lanka at locations including [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [Nuwara Eliya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuwara_Eliya "Nuwara Eliya") and [Galle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galle "Galle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4)

_**Pravegaya**_ (English: velocity ) is a 2015 [Sri Lankan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka") Sinhala action thriller film directed by Donald Jayantha and produced by Sadesh Kumar. It stars [Hemal Ranasinghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemal_Ranasinghe "Hemal Ranasinghe"), and [Udari Perera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udari_Perera "Udari Perera") in lead roles along with [Jayalath Manoratne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayalath_Manoratne "Jayalath Manoratne"), [Pubudu Chathuranga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pubudu_Chathuranga "Pubudu Chathuranga"), and [Jackson Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Anthony "Jackson Anthony") in supporting roles. Music for the film is done by [Bathiya and Santhush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathiya_and_Santhush "Bathiya and Santhush").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-2) It is the 1228th Sri Lankan film in the [Sinhala cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Sri_Lanka "Cinema of Sri Lanka").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-3) The film is a remake of 2007 film _[Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan\_(2007\_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)")_.

## Plot

Hemal is a happy-go-lucky middle-class family guy who spends time playing carrom in the streets with his friends Janith and Kumar. His father and he keep falling into minor misunderstandings, and he indulges in a hopeless romance with a strange girl who he meets at a bus stop. When he is caught in the act of stealing a pittance from his father for booze with his friends, Hemal questions his father’s responsibility towards his upbringing. His angry father gives Hemal some of his savings and tells him to do something with his life. Hemal purchases a [TVS Apache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVS_Apache "TVS Apache") bike instead and finds a job. The bike eventually saves his life from a freak incident and gets lost, subjecting him to interminable anguish as he searches for his bike. When his family members asks him about his bike, he tells them that he has given it for dealer service.

Hemal comes into conflict with the underworld when he witnesses a brutal murder planned by a gang of Smuggling don, Brando and his accomplices. Hemal finds out that his bike was stolen by a petty bike thief who turns out to be in connection with Brando's younger brother G.J.I. Hemal traces down the culprit as Chamara and hands him over to the local police station. A formal complaint is lodged on Chamara on the same night. Later that night Hemal confesses to his family that his bike was stolen. His Family is very upset with him due to his irresponsible behavior. The next morning G.J.I visits Hemal's residence and threatens him to withdraw the complaint against Chamara. When Hemal refuses, a fight breaks between Hemal and G.J.I, where G.J.I is joined by few of his accomplices, Hemal manages to fight them all and leaves G.J.I beaten and embarrassed among the public. Brando returns home in bail after a murder charge. When he finds out what happened to G.J.I, he gets furious and sends his henchmen to kill Hemal without knowing the reason for his brother's embarrassment. Meanwhile, Hemal, along with his friend and auto driver Kumar, meets Brando at his own residence. G.J.I is not home at that time. Hemal tells the truth to Brando but refuses to believe that his brother G.J.I and his men stole his bike. After hearing from his close ally Wasanth, Brando believes Hemal, apologizing for what happened and promises Hemal that he will do whatever he can to get his bike back. But it was too late for Hemal's father Jayalath Manoratne who receives the attack from G.J.I's men. He was admitted in a hospital and Hemal breaks down after knowing that his father may never walk again after his right leg is paralysed by the attack. Brando, G.J.I and their men visit Hemal to condole and apologize for what happened this time. Hemal turns down the apology and again an immediate fight was about to break between Hemal and G.J.I before Brando separates them both. Although he wants to stay away, Hemal invariably gets dragged into rubbing shoulders with the criminals who now target his family to seek revenge.

Hemal's bike was caught by Anti-Narcotics wing police and they nab Hemal suspecting him of Drug-smuggling in his bike. They release him after Hemal tells them that his bike was stolen and shows them his FIR copy. But he doesn't tell them about G.J.I or Brando. Now Hemal learns that his bike was stolen by Brando's men to escape from a murder scene but it was G.J.I who smuggled drugs in his bike's petrol tank. Hemal loses his job as an employee in his workplace since his bike was a source of transportation, and as he was kept at police custody for one night. Hemal also gets despair from Udari's father for being involved unwillingly with Brando's men. G.J.I makes one more attempt at Hemal's life but he was snubbed again by Hemal. Brando becomes unhappy about this and warns him to quit smuggling if he ever gets in Hemal's business anymore. G.J.I accuses Brando of being a non-caring brother and Out intervenes and warns G.J.I to mind his language. Then surprisingly Brando himself comes in support of his brother to lash out at Wasantha. Wasantha separates briefly from Brando after this conflict. The next day Brando and G.J.I gets attacked by unknown gangsters when they were traveling in their car outside the city. Brando asks his brother to stay inside the car and handles the killers on his own. He gets brutally injured though only to find out that he's been stabbed on back by his own Brother G.J.I. The attack was arranged by G.J.I himself to kill Brando. G.J.I delivers the killer blow before telling that Brando is too complacent of Hemal and he's going to kill him after killing Brando. Brando dies. G.J.I creates a scene among Brando's family, henchmen and Wasantha that he's not aware of who launched the assault on Brando. Wasantha gets furious and vows to kill every enemy of his mentor Brando including Hemal.

Hemal gets his bike back and was relieved for a brief time before coming to know what is going on and G.J.I is after him and his family. He first goes to save Udari. After securing her, he goes to save his family. He thinks the only way to stop this is to confront G.J.I himself. he takes down all the men sent by G.J.I who comes in his way. Meanwhile, Hemal's family were chased down in Mahen's auto-rickshaw by G.J.I's men. Hemal finds G.J.I hiding in an Ice-factory and engages him in a fight. Hemal gets G.J.I under the knife, threatening him to ask his men to leave Hemal's family. G.J.I does so. When Heaml is about to leave, G.J.I provokes him to continue the fight until death. Hemal manages to dodge G.J.I's swing of his knife and gets a steel rod to fatally knock down G.J.I. Wasantha arrives at the scene. Surprisingly he tells G.J.I that he discovered G.J.I's conspiracy of killing Brando before G.J.I dies. Hemal leaves the scene in his much beloved Apache bike.

## Background

_Pravegeya_ is an official sinhala remake of the Indian Tamil film [Polladhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polladhavan_(2007_film) "Polladhavan (2007 film)") which starred [Dhanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhanush "Dhanush") and [Divya Spandana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Spandana "Divya Spandana") in its lead roles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4) It is considered to be the most expensive and the biggest budgeted film ever done in Sri Lanka.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Jacqueline Fernandez was cast into a lead role in September 2011 for [Rs.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lankan_rupee "Sri Lankan rupee")8 million which is considered as the highest budget ever been paid to an actress in Sri Lanka,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] however, the production met initial difficulties when Fernandez failed to appear on her initial shooting date. Filming was done in Sri Lanka at locations including [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [Nuwara Eliya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuwara_Eliya "Nuwara Eliya") and [Galle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galle "Galle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dhaulagiri&oldid=957572430#cite_note-Sri_Lanka_Mirror_2-4)
